This is an empirical imaging study that includes a clearly diagnosed bvFTD cohort and reports whole-brain voxelwise analyses. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion (fulltext appears complete). The study used resting-state fMRI for RSN ICA analyses and VBM for grey-matter measurements (I3). It enrolled 15 clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients and 15 healthy controls (I4, I5). Functional and structural data were spatially normalized to Talairach space and group-level, whole-brain contrasts comparing bvFTD to controls are reported (RS-fMRI network differences and VBM results) satisfying I6 and I7; whole-brain results are described in the text and figures (I8). No exclusion criteria apply (not a review, not ROI-only, no disallowed modalities, and sample exclusions not violated). Therefore the paper meets all required inclusion criteria and should be included in the review.

This is a VBM study of clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients with autopsy-confirmed diagnoses and voxel-wise whole-brain analyses. The paper reports voxel-based morphometry (W-score) maps, frequency maps, and linear discriminant voxelwise maps comparing bvFTD patients to controls and presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise results in figures (Figs 3–4) and supplementary material. Sample size for patients with imaging (n=82) exceeds the minimum (≥6). The methods explicitly describe voxel-wise, whole-brain analyses in standard space and comparisons to control data to generate W-scores. Although coordinate tables are not shown in the extracted text, whole-brain voxelwise group results are clearly reported in figures and described in the text, satisfying the requirement for whole-brain, group-level results for the bvFTD group. Full text appears complete.

This empirical study used voxel-based morphometry (VBM) on 3T MRI and reports voxelwise group analyses. The sample includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=19) and healthy controls (n=20), meeting minimum sample-size requirements. The paper reports between-group voxelwise contrasts comparing patient groups (bvFTD and SD) to controls (voxel-wise two-sample t-tests) with results referenced to MNI space and statistical parametric maps/tables presented. Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results for the bvFTD group versus controls are reported (atrophy maps and VBM behavioural correlates). No exclusion criteria apply (not a review, not ROI-only, not DTI/FC-only, and patient sample appears free of excluded comorbidities). Full text appears complete with methods, results, and discussion. Therefore the study meets the review’s inclusion criteria for bvFTD neuroimaging VBM studies.

This study meets all inclusion criteria: (I3) used voxel-based morphometry (VBM) for bvFTD and AD groups; (I4) included clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=21) per revised criteria; (I5) sample sizes meet thresholds (bvFTD n=21; controls n=20); (I6) reported between-group VBM contrasts comparing bvFTD to controls (two-sample t-tests) without pooling bvFTD with other groups; (I7) provided whole-brain, voxelwise group-level results for bvFTD (reported atrophy patterns from VBM, p<0.001 uncorrected, extent threshold=50 voxels); (I8) whole-brain results are described in text and referenced figures/tables/supplementary materials. No exclusion criteria from the list apply. Therefore the study is excluded because it fails to meet I6 (required between-group contrast comparing bvFTD to controls).

This study includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (64 bvFTD cases) and adequate sample size, but it does not meet the imaging-modality and whole-brain voxelwise reporting requirements of the review. The primary analyses use automated regional volumetry/atlas-based regional volumes and derived indices (API, ASI, TPL) rather than VBM, task/resting-state fMRI, or FDG-PET as the main imaging modality (I3 not met). Although an exploratory voxel-based morphometry (VBM) cluster analysis is mentioned, the paper does not present clear whole-brain, standard-space (MNI/Talairach) between-group voxelwise contrasts for the overall bvFTD group versus controls (or clearly tabulated coordinates), so criteria requiring at least one between-group contrast in a defined stereotactic space (I6) and at least one group-level whole-brain voxelwise result from the target sample (I7) are not clearly satisfied. Therefore the study should be excluded for not meeting I3, I6, and I7.

The full text reports resting-state fMRI (rs-fMRI) and diffusion MRI analyses; rs-fMRI (ICA/dual-regression of the DMN) satisfies imaging modality criterion (I3). The sample includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=12) and controls (n=17), meeting I4 and I5 (both groups ≥6). The manuscript reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrasts (Randomise, one-way ANCOVA and post-hoc t-tests) for DMN connectivity and TBSS-based DTI metrics; results are reported as cluster-based whole-brain findings with reference to supplement tables (acceptable per I6 and I8). Whole-brain voxelwise evidence from the target bvFTD group is clearly presented (I7). No exclusion criteria apply: this is an empirical study (not a review), reports whole-brain analyses (not ROI-only), and does not ONLY report seed-based FC, DTI, or cortical thickness (it includes whole-brain rs-fMRI ICA results). Full text appears complete. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample (n=17) and healthy controls (n=22). The study uses task fMRI (satisfying I3), includes a bvFTD group (I4) with >=6 participants and a control group >=6 (I5). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise second-level analyses (SPM) with between-group contrasts and syndrome-specific results described for bvFTD versus controls (e.g., reduced posterior middle temporal and fusiform activation), meeting I6 and I7. Results are presented as whole-brain SPMs and described in the text/figures (I8). The full text provided includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, and appears complete for screening. No exclusion criteria are met.

This study meets all imaging and sample criteria for inclusion. It reports voxel-based morphometry (VBM) whole-brain analyses aligned to the MNI152 standard (explicitly stated), using voxelwise general linear models and permutation-based testing with familywise-error correction; results are presented as group-level whole-brain clusters (figures and supplementary tables referenced). The sample comprises clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD patients (58 meeting inclusion criteria) and a control group, both clearly reported and large enough (>6 participants). Between-group voxelwise contrasts comparing bvFTD to controls are described and localized in MNI space. No exclusion criteria apply (not a review, not ROI-only, empirical dataset, not solely seed-based FC/DTI/cortical thickness). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study meets I3 (VBM used), I4 (clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample), I5 (n=25 bvFTD, n=21 controls), I7 (reports group-level voxelwise VBM results derived from the target bvFTD sample) and I8 (results presented in tables/figures). However, it does not report a between-group voxelwise contrast directly comparing bvFTD versus controls in MNI/Talairach space (no whole-brain bvFTD>control or control>bvFTD contrast is presented), so inclusion criterion I6 is not satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) are met. Full text appears complete.

It does use FDG-PET (I3 satisfied) but does not present a diagnostically defined bvFTD sample with n≥6, nor any between-group voxelwise contrasts in MNI/Talairach space, nor whole-brain voxelwise group-level results. Therefore it fails I4, I5, I6, and I7. The manuscript appears non-empirical/methods/report-style rather than reporting original quantitative group analyses (E8 applies). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical, whole-brain VBM study that explicitly includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=45) and healthy controls (n=35). The study used voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (I3), includes bvFTD participants (I4) with sufficient sample size (I5), reports pairwise between-group voxelwise contrasts comparing bvFTD to controls (I6), and presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise results (figures/tables) in standard space (MNI) (I7). No exclusion criteria are met (e.g., not a review/meta-analysis, not ROI-only, not seed FC/DTI/cortical thickness only), and the full text provided includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This empirical study uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) as the imaging modality and reports whole-brain, voxelwise comparisons of bvFTD patients (two bvFTD subgroups) versus healthy controls. Participants meet clinical bvFTD criteria (revised criteria) and group sizes are sufficient (34 bvFTD patients; 30 controls). The manuscript describes whole-brain VBM contrasts (AbvFTD vs controls; DbvFTD vs controls; AbvFTD vs DbvFTD) with FDR-corrected results and refers to Supplementary Table/Figure for VBM findings (coordinate tables/figures reported). Thus inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical VBM study of clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients with adequate sample sizes and whole-brain voxelwise results. The paper uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) on MRI (Methods: VBM, SPM8), includes clinically diagnosed probable/possible/pre-bvFTD patients confirmed at follow-up (n=194 total; VBM subset: 44 probable bvFTD, 19 possible bvFTD, 14 pre-bvFTD) and healthy controls (n=36). The study reports between-group whole-brain contrasts (probable bvFTD < HC; possible bvFTD < HC; pre-bvFTD < HC) with stereotactic coordinates for significant clusters (x,y,z values provided) and familywise error correction at whole-brain level. No exclusion criteria are met (not a review, not ROI-only, not non-empirical, no disallowed imaging modality). Therefore all relevant inclusion criteria are satisfied and the study should be included in the review.

This study meets all inclusion criteria: it uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) on structural MRI (I3); includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample (52 patients, diagnosed per current criteria) (I4); has adequate sample sizes (52 patients, 52 controls) (I5); reports between-group voxelwise contrasts comparing bvFTD to controls in MNI space (I6); presents whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results (voxelwise GLM, FWE-corrected) clearly identified as from the target bvFTD sample (I7); and reports results in figures/tables/coordinates as described (I8). This is an original empirical study of clinically diagnosed bvFTD (N=63) using voxel-based morphometry/voxelwise grey-matter analyses (ANTs preprocessing, FSL randomise) comparing bvFTD to healthy controls (N=55). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results (clusters, peak loci reported in MNI/Talairach space, FWE-corrected clusters and coordinate tables/figures) relating baseline GM density to longitudinal cognitive decline. All required imaging and reporting criteria for inclusion are met, and no exclusion criteria apply (not a review, not ROI-only, not seed-based FC/DTI/cortical-thickness-only). Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and appears complete.

No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) apply. Full text appears complete.

This empirical study reports voxelwise, whole-brain SPM analyses of both 18F-FDG PET and voxel-based morphometry (GM density) comparing a bvFTD patient group to healthy controls. It used SPM8 with customized templates, reports Talairach-corrected coordinates and cluster-level inference, and presents group-level between-group contrasts for the whole bvFTD sample and bvFTD subgroups (bvFTD+ and bvFTD−) vs controls. Sample sizes meet thresholds (25 patients, 20 controls). The bvFTD group is not pooled with other patient groups. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not a review, not ROI-only, not non-empirical, no disallowed imaging-only methods, and no comorbid psychiatric/other dementia confounds). Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8.

The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrasts and regression results (with family-wise error correction, TFCE) and references peak voxels summarized in table e-1 (supplement), satisfying requirements for reporting coordinates/whole-brain results. No exclusion criteria are met (not a review; not ROI-only; no disallowed modalities). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria I3,I4,I5,I6,I7,I8 and none of the exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical, full-text MRI volumetric study that included clinically diagnosed bvFTD participants (I4) with adequate group sizes (I5). Exclusion criterion met: E6. Full text appears complete.

I3 (VBM modality), I4 (includes bvFTD sample), and I5 (adequate sample size overall and implied per-group sizes) are satisfied. Full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) were met.

Exclusion (E6) applies: the study performs ROI-based network analyses using AAL parcellation and MST on regionwise wavelet correlation matrices; it does not report voxelwise, whole-brain group-level results in a stereotactic coordinate space (MNI/Talairach). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (resting-state fMRI used), I4 (clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample), I5 (n=41 bvFTD, n=39 controls). Although the paper includes VBM (I3), clinically diagnosed bvFTD participants (I4, n=20), and adequate sample sizes for patient and control groups (I5), it does NOT report any between-group, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts comparing the bvFTD group to healthy controls in a defined stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach). This is a genetic/clinical case series of TBK1 mutation carriers that includes several patients with behavioural-variant FTD and used FDG-PET in two patients (so I3, I4, and I5 are met: FDG-PET modality present; study includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients; there are ≥6 FTD patients in the cohort). However, the paper does not report any group-level between-group voxelwise contrasts in a standard stereotaxic space (MNI/Talairach) comparing a bvFTD group to healthy controls, nor any whole-brain, voxelwise group results or coordinate tables/figures suitable for meta-analysis. Therefore it fails I6 and I7. Because no whole-brain group results are provided, it falls under the exclusion of studies without whole-brain results (E6). Full text appears complete.

The study meets the meta-analysis objective and all required inclusion criteria: I3 (uses voxel-based morphometry), I4 (includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD participants within the sample), I5 (bvFTD subgroup size = 12; controls = 30, both ≥6), I6 (reports between-group VBM contrasts comparing bvFTD group to controls in SPM/MNI space), I7 (reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results for the bvFTD subgroup), and I8 (results are described in text and shown in figures). The full text reports empirical neuroimaging data in a clinically diagnosed bvFTD cohort using voxel-based morphometry and task-based fMRI (satisfies I3). This study meets I3 (uses VBM, resting-state fMRI, and 18F-FDG PET), I4 (includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients; n=11), and I5 (bvFTD group size ≥6). However, it does not meet I6 or I7: there is no healthy/control group reported for between-group contrasts versus bvFTD, and the paper does not present group-level whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (in MNI/Talairach space) comparing bvFTD to controls. Analyses are restricted to predefined ROI cores (voxelwise measures within those ROIs) and multivariate SVM classification; results are reported as classification accuracies rather than whole-brain coordinate-based between-group contrasts. Therefore the study reports only ROI-limited results with no qualifying whole-brain group contrasts and falls under exclusion E6 (only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study uses FDG-PET imaging and includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (I3, I4) with sample size meeting minimum (bvFTD n=13) (I5). However, it does not report any between-group voxelwise results in a defined stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) comparing bvFTD to controls, nor any group-level whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps or coordinate tables. PET data are reported as region-level qualitative ratings (absent/mild/moderate/severe) and correlations with regional hypometabolism, which constitute regional/ROI-style reporting rather than whole-brain voxelwise results. Therefore inclusion criteria I6 and I7 are not met, and exclusion criterion E6 (studies reporting only ROI/region-level analyses with no whole-brain results) applies. Full text appears complete. Result: EXCLUDED.

This is an empirical study using resting-state fMRI and voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (I3). It includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=21) and healthy controls (n=33), satisfying sample size requirements (I4, I5). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise VBM group contrasts (FWE-corrected t-maps) comparing bvFTD subgroups to controls in MNI-normalized space (I6, I7), and presents results in the text/figures with supplementary tables (I8). The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met: it is not a review/meta-analysis, includes whole-brain results (not ROI-only), is empirical, and does not rely solely on seed-based FC/DTI/cortical thickness. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This study used VBM (I3), included a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=13, I4), and had adequate sample sizes for patients and controls (bvFTD n=13; controls n=20, I5). However, the VBM analyses reported are correlational within a combined patient cohort and significant effects were reported only within pre-specified regions of interest; no between-group voxelwise contrasts comparing bvFTD versus controls in standard stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) are presented, and no whole-brain group-level voxelwise results for the bvFTD group are reported. Therefore inclusion criteria I6 and I7 are not met. This meets exclusion criterion E6 (reports only ROI findings / no qualifying whole-brain results). Full text appears complete.

The full text reports whole-brain voxelwise VBM analyses (grey matter density maps, SPM5) and regression analyses mapped to MNI space, satisfying imaging modality requirements. The sample includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=14) and healthy controls (imaging contrasts vs. controls), meeting sample requirements (≥6 participants per group). The paper reports between-group voxelwise contrasts for bvFTD versus controls (separate from other patient groups) and whole-brain results described in the text/figures/tables. No exclusion criteria are violated (not a review; not ROI-only; empirical VBM study; no disallowed modalities). The provided full text includes introduction, methods, imaging methods, results and discussion and appears complete for screening purposes.

The study meets all specified inclusion criteria: it uses whole-brain voxel-based morphometry (VBM) analyses (I3), includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=49) (I4) and healthy controls (n=27) with adequate sample sizes (I5). The paper reports between-group whole-brain voxelwise contrasts comparing each FTD subtype (including bvFTD) to healthy controls and presents anatomical results in MNI space (I6,I7). Results/figures and coordinate descriptions of atrophy maps and VBM clusters are provided (I8). No exclusion criteria are met: this is an empirical original study (not a review), it reports whole-brain VBM rather than only ROI or seed-based FC/DTI/cortical thickness results, and there is no indication of disqualifying comorbid psychiatric or substance-abuse samples. The full text is complete with methods, results and neuroimaging data. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical VBM study that explicitly includes 51 clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD (bv-FTD) patients and 14 healthy controls (both groups >6). The study used voxel-based morphometry (SPM5) and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses comparing bv-FTD to controls, with significant clusters described and referenced supplementary table e-1 (coordinates/cluster data reported in main/supplemental materials). The methods, results, and discussion contain whole-brain voxelwise findings associated with executive-function components in the bv-FTD group. No exclusion criteria are met (not a review, not ROI-only, not non-empirical, not an FC/DTI/cortical-thickness-only study, and no disqualifying comorbidities are reported). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore all relevant inclusion criteria (I3,I4,I5,I6,I7,I8) are satisfied.

This study uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (I3) and includes a clinically diagnosed frontal-variant FTD group (FTD-fv, equivalent to bvFTD) (I4). Patient group sizes meet the minimum (25 FTD-fv patients; 22 CBS; controls n=14) (I5). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrasts comparing the FTD-fv group to controls with results reported in MNI coordinates (e.g., crosshair 14,10,14) and FWE-corrected maps (I6, I7). Whole-brain results are presented in figures and described in text (I8). Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided here, so fulltext_incomplete=false. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical clinical study of behavioral-variant FTD with >6 patients (63 FTD cases) so it meets I4 (bvFTD sample) and I5 (sample size ≥6). However, it does not meet key imaging and analysis criteria required by the review. Although PET and MRI/SPECT were used, the paper reports clinical (visual) interpretations of structural MRI and SPECT/PET and does not report voxelwise whole-brain analyses (no VBM, no task or resting fMRI, and no coordinate-based FDG-PET results). There are no group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) results reported in MNI/Talairach space or coordinate tables/figures. Therefore I3, I6, and I7 (and related I8) are not satisfied. This violates the review’s requirement for whole-brain voxelwise coordinate results; accordingly the study is excluded under E6 (no whole-brain voxelwise results/only non-voxel clinical imaging interpretations). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical VBM study of clinically diagnosed bvFTD with adequate sample sizes (15 patients per bvFTD stage; 45 controls), reporting whole-brain voxelwise (SPM/VBM) group contrasts with MNI coordinates and corrected statistics. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8. However, multiple participants across bvFTD groups had coexisting motor neuron disease (MND) (e.g., 5/15 in CDR 0.5, 5/15 in CDR 1, 3/15 in CDR 2–3), meaning the sample includes concurrent neurological disease. This violates exclusion criterion E7 (studies including participants with other neurological symptoms). The full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion). Because any single exclusion criterion mandates exclusion, the study is excluded.

This is an empirical VBM study of bvFTD that reports whole-brain voxelwise group contrasts and correlations in standard coordinate space. The paper uses voxel‑based morphometry (VBM) as the imaging modality, includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (N=20 total; N=17 in MRI subset) and healthy controls (N=39 total; N=28 MRI subset), and both patient and control groups exceed the 6‑participant threshold. The authors report VBM atrophy contrasts comparing bvFTD to controls and report voxelwise clusters with coordinates (MNI/Talairach) for both masked reward‑network and whole‑brain analyses. Whole‑brain voxelwise results are clearly described in the text and include coordinate data. Full text contains methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

The study is excluded because it does not meet all required inclusion criteria I6 and I7. Met inclusion criteria: I3 (uses fMRI and voxel-based morphometry), I4 (includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients), and I5 (bvFTD group and controls meet minimum n≥6). Not met: I6 and I7 — the voxelwise structural MRI analyses combined bvFTD and PNFA into a single group for patient vs control comparisons, and no group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) contrast exclusively comparing bvFTD to controls in MNI/Talairach space is reported. The fMRI component was performed in healthy young adults only and does not provide bvFTD vs control whole-brain contrasts. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) were triggered. Full text appears complete.

This study includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (part of a 72-patient cohort), uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) and task-free resting-state fMRI, and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise atrophy analyses and maps derived in standard space (voxelwise W-score maps referenced to a healthy control sample). Sample sizes for patient and control groups exceed the minimum (patients n=72; structural controls n=288; functional controls n=75). The paper presents group-level whole-brain results clearly attributed to bvFTD (and svPPA) and provides voxelwise/atlas-based analyses suitable for coordinate/voxelwise extraction. Full article content including methods, results, and discussion is present. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria apply.

This study is excluded because it does not meet the meta-analysis imaging or sample and whole-brain results requirements. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (patient group size: 12 tvFTD patients and imaging controls ≥6). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the paper is not eligible for inclusion in this meta-analysis.

Although this study used VBM and FDG-PET and reports whole-brain voxelwise group analyses, it is excluded because it does not provide bvFTD-specific between-group contrasts. The FTLD patient sample (n=11) is a mixed group (FTD n=4, semantic dementia n=5, mixed n=2) and results are reported for the pooled FTLD group versus controls rather than for a clinically defined bvFTD (behavioral-variant FTD) subgroup. Therefore: (a) I6 is not satisfied (no between-group contrast specifically for bvFTD vs. controls in stereotactic coordinates); (b) I4 is not satisfied (bvFTD diagnosis is not clearly isolated/present as a target sample); (c) I5 is not satisfied for a bvFTD subgroup because the FTD subgroup has only 4 patients (<6). Inclusion criteria satisfied: I3 (VBM/FDG-PET used), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise results reported), I8 (results clearly described in text/figures). No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) applied. Full text appears complete.

This study is excluded because it does not meet the imaging-modality and whole-brain/coordinate reporting requirements of the meta-analysis. This study meets all inclusion criteria for the review objective. It used voxel-based morphometry (VBM) as an imaging modality and explicitly reports VBM analyses (I3). This study meets the review objective and all required inclusion criteria. This is an empirical VBM study that includes a clinically diagnosed FTD group defined by Neary criteria (behavioral variant features) and compares them to controls. Imaging modality is voxel-based morphometry on T1 MRI (I3). This is an empirical VBM study of autopsy-confirmed FTLD that reports whole-brain, voxelwise comparisons including analyses restricted to clinically diagnosed bvFTD subjects versus matched controls. The study reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level results for bvFTD subjects compared to controls (VBM results shown on template surface and coronal slices, corrected for multiple comparisons), satisfying whole-brain evidence (I7) and providing results in figures/voxel space as described in text (I6, I8). Sample size is 15 bvFTD patients and 15 matched healthy controls (>=6 each). The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. This VBM study includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD participants (19 bvFTD cases) and sufficient sample sizes (19 patients, 22 controls) and reports voxelwise SPMs/coordinates. This is a task-based fMRI study of clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=15) versus healthy controls (n=11). This is an empirical, longitudinal FDG-PET study of ‘frontal variant’ FTD (behavioral variant phenotype). The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the bvFTD meta-analysis.

Inclusion criteria met: I3 (uses VBM), I5 (patient group N=30 FTD and control N=14 meet sample size), I7 (reports whole-brain voxelwise SPM analyses), I8 (whole-brain results presented as statistical maps/figures). This study uses VBM and compares ALS-FTD patients to controls with whole-brain voxelwise results in MNI space, and sample sizes exceed 6 per group. Inclusion criterion I4 (bvFTD or Pick’s disease sample) is not clearly met. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) apply. Therefore the study is excluded because it does not unambiguously sample bvFTD patients (I4 not met).

This study uses FDG-PET (I3), includes a frontal-variant/bvFTD patient group (fv-FTD) (I4), has adequate sample sizes (fv-FTD n=18; controls n=18) (I5), and reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level correlations for the fv-FTD group (SPM results reported in tables/figures) (I7,I8). No exclusion criteria from the list (E5–E9) are triggered. Therefore the study fails to meet all required inclusion criteria (specifically I6) and must be excluded.

This is an empirical study of clinically diagnosed behavioural variant FTD (bvFTD) that uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) as the imaging modality and reports whole-brain, voxelwise group contrasts with MNI coordinates. Sample sizes meet thresholds (bvFTD N=26 overall; imaging subset bvFTD N=21, controls N=12; controls N=16 overall). No exclusion criteria apply (not a review, not ROI-only, no excluded imaging modalities, and sample does not include confounding psychiatric or substance-abuse cases). Full text is complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables). Therefore it meets all required inclusion criteria for the review.

This study uses resting-state fMRI (meets I3), includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients within the sample (7/14; meets I4), has adequate group sizes (FTD n=14, controls n≥6; meets I5), and reports whole-brain voxelwise results with coordinates/figures in MNI space (meets I7 and I8). However, all reported between-group analyses compare the combined FTD-GRN+ group (which mixes bvFTD and avPPA cases) to controls; the paper does not present a bvFTD-only versus controls whole-brain contrast (i.e., the bvFTD group is pooled with other patients). Therefore it fails to meet I6, which requires between-group contrasts where the bvFTD group is not pooled. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) are triggered. Full text appears complete. This study uses VBM and includes adequate sample sizes (FTD n=37, controls present), but does not clearly meet key inclusion criteria for this bvFTD-focused review. Specifically, the FTD sample is not clearly described as clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD (only 4/37 explicitly described as behavioural variant), so I4 is not satisfied. The full text does not report any between-group voxelwise contrast coordinates in a defined stereotactic space (MNI or Talairach), nor does it present clearly a group-level whole-brain voxelwise result in stereotactic coordinates; therefore I6 and I7 are not satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) are triggered. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (VBM used) and I5 (sample sizes >=6). Inclusion criteria not met: I4, I6, I7. Consequently the study is excluded.

This empirical study used voxel-based morphometry (VBM) and explicitly included a behavioral variant FTD (bvFTD) cohort (n=10) alongside healthy controls (n=10). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise contrasts between each disease group (including bvFTD) and controls, with results presented in template/MNI space (and in figures/tables). All required inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply. The provided full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext is complete.

The study does not meet imaging-modality and whole-brain voxelwise reporting requirements for the review. It used volumetric MRI segmentation (Expectation-Maximization segmentation of T1/T2/PD) rather than VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET (fails I3). Exclusion criterion E6 applies because the paper reports regional (lobar) volumetry without whole-brain voxelwise results.
