The study is excluded because it does not report a whole-brain (voxel-wise) between-group contrast that directly compares a clinically-diagnosed bvFTD group (symptomatic carriers only) to controls. Voxel-wise analyses reported in the paper compare mutation carriers (which include both symptomatic and asymptomatic carriers) versus non-carriers rather than a bvFTD-only group. Although the paper includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients and meets several inclusion criteria (see below), the key criteria I6 and I7 are not satisfied: there is no voxel-wise, whole-brain contrast explicitly for the bvFTD (symptomatic) group vs controls—only ROI-based group comparisons among symptomatic, asymptomatic, and controls were reported. Therefore it cannot be included in the meta-analysis focused on whole-brain bvFTD vs control contrasts.

This study meets all required inclusion criteria for the bvFTD imaging meta-analysis. Imaging modality: voxel‑based morphometry (VBM) was used (I3). Sample: includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=24) and healthy controls (n=23), meeting minimum group sizes (I4, I5). Whole‑brain, voxelwise VBM comparisons were performed between patient groups and controls (bvFTD vs controls reported) and between AD and bvFTD, with cluster-level results reported and corrected (whole‑brain evidence) (I6, I7). Results include MNI coordinates for at least some voxelwise findings and supplementary material is referenced, satisfying acceptable reporting formats (I8). No exclusion criteria are met: this is an empirical, original VBM study (not a review), it reports whole‑brain analyses (not ROI‑only), and comorbidities/alcohol abuse were exclusionary in participant selection. Full text appears complete.

This study uses VBM and reports whole-brain voxel-wise comparisons between genetic FTD mutation carriers and noncarriers, and has adequate group sizes. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (VBM used), I5 (>=6 patients and controls), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise results reported), I8 (results reported in figures/tables). However, the meta-analysis targets bvFTD (behavioral variant FTD) specifically. This paper studies genetic FTD mutation carriers (mixed clinical phenotypes) and does not present a group explicitly defined and analyzed as bvFTD alone; thus I4 (bvFTD or Pick’s disease sample) is not satisfied. Also I6 (between-group contrast specifically comparing a bvFTD group to controls, unpooled with other patient groups) is not satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) apply. Full text appears complete. Therefore exclude because the target diagnostic group (bvFTD) is not specifically reported or isolated in the voxelwise contrasts.

This study is excluded because it does not report group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results comparing bvFTD (FTD) patients to controls in stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (uses VBM/SPM voxel-based morphometry), I4 (includes clinically diagnosed FTD corresponding to bvFTD; n=20), I5 (patient group n≥6 and control group n≥6: 20 FTD, 13 controls). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I6 (no clear between-group voxelwise contrast reported for the bvFTD group vs controls in defined stereotactic space) and I7 (no clearly identified group-level whole-brain voxelwise result from the target bvFTD sample; results are presented as single-subject NBVR/SPMs and diagnostic accuracy metrics rather than group-level coordinate tables). No exclusion criteria from the list apply.

This study meets all required inclusion criteria for the bvFTD imaging meta-analysis. It includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=22) and healthy controls (n=34), both >6 participants. The paper performed voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (I3) with scans registered to MNI152 space and voxelwise whole-brain analyses (I7), reporting patient–control group comparisons (bvFTD vs. controls) that replicated the visual-rating findings; these results are referenced in the main text and in supplementary figures (I8). The VBM contrasts were conducted in standard space (MNI) and involve between-group contrasts where bvFTD is not pooled with other patient groups (I6). Sample sizes satisfy I5 and clinical diagnosis criteria satisfy I4. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) are met. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; supplementary figures are externally linked but acceptable, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is an empirical VBM study of clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (23 patients included) with a healthy control group (20 controls). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise VBM group comparisons (two-sample t-test) showing atrophic clusters in bilateral anterior temporal lobes and additional regions, and voxelwise regression analyses relating behavioral measures to GM volume in the patient group. Imaging modality includes VBM (and FDG-PET performed in most patients). Sample sizes exceed the minimum (patients=23, controls=20). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results comparing bvFTD to controls are reported. Full text contains Introduction, Methods (including VBM preprocessing and statistics), Results (behavior and imaging) and Discussion; core article content is present. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, I7 and the reporting allowance I8. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) apply. Full text appears complete.

This study uses resting-state fMRI (dynamic connectivity) and includes clinically diagnosed FTD with a large bvFTD subgroup (n=81), satisfying imaging and sample-size criteria. However, it does not include a healthy control group or report any between-group voxelwise contrasts in MNI/Talairach space comparing the bvFTD group to controls; results are reported as metastate/dynamic connectivity metrics derived from ICA components rather than group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) coordinate-based contrasts. Therefore inclusion criteria I6 and I7 are not met. No exclusion criteria (E5, E6, E7, E8, E9) are specifically triggered by the full text provided.

This study does not meet the review’s target-sample criterion. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (uses FDG-PET) and I5 (patient and control group sizes ≥6: FTLD N=14, controls N=13). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 — participants are described as ‘‘FTLD’’ (frontotemporal lobar degeneration) without specifying behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) or Pick’s disease, so the target diagnostic group (bvFTD/Pick’s) is not clearly present; I6 — there are no reported between-group voxelwise contrasts in MNI/Talairach space specifically comparing a bvFTD group to controls (the paper used SVM classification and ROI coordinates drawn from prior meta-analyses rather than reporting new bvFTD-specific voxelwise coordinate contrasts); I7 — although whole-brain SVM weight maps are presented for FTLD vs. controls, they are not clearly identified as coming from a clinically-diagnosed bvFTD sample. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) apply. Full text appears complete.

This study used Voxel-Based Morphometry (VBM) (satisfies I3) and includes patient groups with >6 participants (AD n=18; SV-PPA n=10) (satisfies I5). However, it does NOT include clinically diagnosed behavioral variant FTD (bvFTD) or Pick’s disease patients (I4 not met). The VBM analysis reported is a group-level whole-brain analysis, but it was performed on controls and AD patients only (25 NC, 7 AD); SV-PPA patients were excluded from the VBM analysis. Therefore there are no between-group contrasts or whole-brain voxelwise results comparing a bvFTD/Pick’s group to controls (I6 and I7 not met). No exclusion criteria from the review list apply. Because the paper does not include the target patient population (bvFTD/Pick’s) and provides no bvFTD whole-brain contrasts, it must be excluded.

Full text is complete and the study is empirical, uses FDG-PET and includes clinically diagnosed frontal variant/bvFTD patients (n=13) and controls (n=21). It reports whole-brain voxelwise SPM results correlating autobiographical memory measures with resting FDG uptake in the fv-FTD group (i.e., group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results in stereotactic space). However, the paper does not present a between-group voxelwise contrast (bvFTD patients versus controls) reported in MNI/Talairach coordinates. Inclusion criterion I6 (at least one between-group contrast comparing bvFTD to controls in defined stereotactic space) is not met, so the study must be excluded. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) apply.

Full text is complete. This fMRI resting-state study includes clinically diagnosed FTD patients (including 18 bvFTD cases) and reports whole-brain voxelwise ICA results correlating Reserve Index with functional connectivity. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (resting-state fMRI), I4 (sample includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD cases), I5 (patient subgroup size ≥6), I8 (results reported with MNI coordinates/voxelwise clusters). However, it does NOT meet I6: the paper does not report any between-group contrast comparing a bvFTD group to healthy controls (bvFTD results are not presented as a distinct between-group contrast against controls). Consequently I7 is not met for the target comparison: there are no group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results clearly identified as coming from a bvFTD vs control contrast. Because both I6 and I7 are required, the study must be excluded.

Inclusion criteria met: I3 — the study used voxelwise gray-matter analyses with SPM2 (a VBM-style, whole-brain approach). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I4 — the sample is a mixed/pathologically defined FTD spectrum (tau-positive, tau-negative, fv-AD) and does not specifically report a clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) or Pick’s disease group; I5 — the imaging subgroup is small (total n=12: tau-positive n=5; tau-negative n=4; fv-AD n=3), so patient-group sizes for the imaging results are <6; I6 — the reported between-group contrasts are pathology-defined groups vs controls, not a bvFTD vs control contrast (bvFTD group is not isolated); I7 — although whole-brain voxelwise results are reported, they are not identified as coming from a clinically defined bvFTD sample. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) are clearly met. Full text appears complete.

Full text is a complete empirical MRI volumetry study of basal forebrain in FTD. Exclusion criteria met: E6 (study reports region-of-interest/volumetric analyses with no whole-brain, voxelwise results). Inclusion criteria met: I4 (includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients) and I5 (patient and control groups both >6 participants). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I3 (does NOT use VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET; it uses T1 volumetric segmentation/GIF), I6 (no reported between-group contrast results in a defined stereotactic space [MNI/Talairach] comparing bvFTD voxelwise to controls), and I7 (no whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results). Because E6 is met and key inclusion criteria I3, I6, and I7 are not satisfied, the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This is a longitudinal volumetric MRI study using semi-automated whole-brain and ventricular atrophy measures (BBSI, VBSI), not VBM, task/resting fMRI, or FDG-PET. Although the sample includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (11 bvFTD) and sufficient sample sizes with controls, the paper does not report any voxelwise, whole-brain group-level results in a defined stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) or coordinate tables comparing bvFTD to controls. Therefore it fails key inclusion criteria requiring modality (I3) and voxelwise whole-brain results (I6, I7). No exclusion criteria from the list are directly met.

This study uses Voxel-Based Morphometry (VBM) and reports whole-brain voxelwise correlational results across genetic FTD mutation groups, but it does not include or specifically report results from a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group compared directly against healthy controls. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (VBM used) and I5 (patient group size ≥6). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (does not explicitly present a clinically diagnosed bvFTD or Pick’s disease patient group), I6 (no between-group contrast comparing a bvFTD group to controls), and I7 (no group-level whole-brain result clearly identified as coming from a bvFTD target sample). No exclusion criteria from the list are triggered. Therefore the article does not satisfy the review’s requirement to provide bvFTD vs. control voxelwise between-group contrasts and must be excluded.

The study uses VBM and includes sufficient sample sizes, but it does not specifically report results for clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) distinct from other FTD variants, nor does it present a clear between-group voxelwise contrast of bvFTD versus controls unpooled with other patient groups. Therefore it fails key inclusion criteria I4, I6 and I7.

The full text reports voxelwise whole-brain analyses (VBM and TBSS aligned to MNI space) comparing a clinical bvFTD group to controls. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (uses VBM), I4 (includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients, n=13), I5 (patient group n≥6 and control group n≥6; HCbvFTD n=25), I6 (reports between-group contrasts in MNI-standard space comparing bvFTD to controls), I7 (reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise results for the bvFTD group), and I8 (results shown in figures/supplementary and described in text). No exclusion criteria apply: this is an original empirical study (not a review), it contains whole-brain voxelwise results (not ROI-only), and although it includes DTI measures, it also includes VBM (an allowed modality). Full text appears complete with introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED for the meta-analysis objective.

This study is excluded because it does not meet the imaging-modality and whole-brain voxelwise reporting requirements of the review. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (study includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients) and I5 (bvFTD patient group size in the cohort exceeds 6). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (no VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET analyses — only structural MRI described), I6 (no between-group voxelwise contrasts reported in MNI/Talairach space comparing bvFTD to controls), I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise results provided), I8 (no coordinate tables/figures of whole-brain results). No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) appear to apply. Full text appears complete. Therefore the paper cannot be included in this coordinate-based whole-brain imaging meta-analysis.

The study is excluded because it does not provide the required bvFTD-specific, whole-brain voxelwise between-group results in standard space. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (uses 18F-FDG PET imaging) and I5 (FTD patient group size = 36, ≥6). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (paper reports FTD patients but does not present results specifically for clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD / Pick’s disease as a distinct target group), I6 (no clearly reported between-group contrast in MNI or Talairach space comparing bvFTD to controls), and I7 (no clearly presented whole-brain group-level voxelwise coordinates/maps attributable to a bvFTD vs control contrast in the main text; supplemental material not provided here). No exclusion criteria from E5–E9 are directly triggered based on the available full text. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This study is excluded because it does not meet the imaging- and analysis-specific inclusion criteria required for the meta-analysis. It used structural MRI distance measures (FA index and frontal atrophy percentages) rather than VBM, fMRI (resting/task), or FDG-PET (I3 not met). It does not report any whole-brain, voxelwise group-level results nor stereotactic coordinates (MNI/Talairach) from between-group contrasts (I6 and I7 not met). The sample does meet the minimum size requirement (41 patients, 121 comparison subjects; I5 met), but the paper does not explicitly specify behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) or Pick’s disease as the target diagnostic subgroup (I4 not clearly met). Because the manuscript reports region-based measures/indices without whole-brain voxelwise results, it falls under exclusion E6 (ROI/region-only analyses with no whole-brain results).

This is an empirical VBM study (voxel-based morphometry) with accompanying whole-brain voxelwise analyses comparing clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients to healthy controls. The sample includes 13 bvFTD patients and 19 controls (both >6). Methods state images were normalized to MNI space and voxelwise two-sample t-tests were performed; Results explicitly include a section “Voxel-wise comparisons between bvFTD and CN” reporting whole-brain findings. The paper therefore meets modality (VBM), target sample (bvFTD), sample size, and whole-brain between-group contrast requirements. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion; no exclusion criteria are met (not a review; not ROI-only; no disallowed comorbid sample; not DTI-only). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical study using voxel-based morphometry (VBM) to compare clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=33) with healthy controls (n=34). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise two-sample t-tests were performed in MNI space with results reported (figures and supplementary tables of coordinates) for bvFTD versus controls; cerebellar analyses used SUIT but whole-brain VBM results for the cerebral cortex are presented. The bvFTD group was not pooled with other patient groups in the reported between-group contrasts. Sample sizes exceed the minimum. Therefore all required inclusion criteria for VBM studies of bvFTD are met and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical study that includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients and uses both VBM and task-based fMRI, with patient and control group sizes >6. However, the imaging group-level voxelwise contrasts reported are comparisons between AD and bvFTD (VBM) rather than between bvFTD and healthy controls. The paper does not present a whole-brain (voxelwise) group contrast explicitly comparing bvFTD to controls in MNI/Talairach space. Therefore it fails inclusion criteria I6 (between-group contrast of bvFTD vs controls) and I7 (at least one group-level whole-brain result clearly identified as coming from the bvFTD vs control comparison). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (VBM/fMRI used), I4 (bvFTD sample), I5 (sample sizes ≥6). No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) apply. Full text appears complete. Given the missing required between-group whole-brain contrast comparing bvFTD to controls, the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This study uses whole-brain VBM and reports group-wise voxelwise neuroimaging results for a C9ORF72 mutation FTLD group (n=11) versus controls, but it does not provide a group-level, whole-brain contrast specifically comparing a clinically diagnosed bvFTD (behavioral-variant FTD) patient group to healthy controls. (a) Exclusion IDs met: none. (b) Inclusion IDs met: I3 (uses VBM), I5 (patient group n=11 and controls n=15, both ≥6). (c) Inclusion IDs not met: I4 (the analyzed patient group is defined by C9ORF72 mutation and is heterogeneous in clinical syndrome rather than a clinically defined bvFTD/Pick’s group), I6 (no between-group contrast reported that specifically compares a bvFTD-only group to controls), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise results are not explicitly reported as coming from a bvFTD target sample). Full text appears complete. Therefore the paper does not meet all required inclusion criteria for the bvFTD-focused meta-analysis.

This study is a retrospective clinical case series that used 18F-FDG PET (with/without 11C-PIB) and included clinically diagnosed FTD patients (behavioral variant criteria applied) with n=7, so it satisfies I3 (FDG-PET used), I4 (bvFTD included), and I5 (patient group size ≥6). However, it does NOT report any between-group voxelwise contrasts comparing bvFTD to healthy controls in a defined stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach), nor does it provide group-level whole-brain voxelwise results or coordinate tables. Therefore it fails I6 and I7 and does not provide the required whole-brain statistical data for inclusion in the meta-analysis. No exclusion criteria from the provided list are directly met. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This study uses FDG-PET and includes clinically diagnosed FTD cases (including behavioral-variant descriptions), but it does not meet the meta-analysis requirements. The paper reports expert visual reads and diagnostic concordance metrics; it does not present any voxelwise, whole-brain group-level analyses in a stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) comparing a bvFTD group to healthy controls, nor does it provide coordinate tables or between-group statistical contrasts. Subgroup counts for bvFTD are not clearly reported, so the required sample-size criterion for the target patient group cannot be verified. Therefore it fails inclusion criteria I5 (insufficient/unclear patient-group counts), I6 (no between-group stereotactic contrasts), I7 (no whole-brain voxelwise group-level results), and I8 (no coordinate/voxelwise results in text/tables). Included criteria met: I3 (FDG-PET), I4 (includes clinically diagnosed FTD/bvFTD). No exclusion criteria from the list clearly apply. Full text appears complete for assessment.

This study uses T1-weighted hippocampal subfield volumetry (automated FreeSurfer/GIF segmentation), not VBM, fMRI, or FDG‑PET, so it does not meet modality requirement (I3). It reports regional (hippocampal subfield) volume comparisons rather than voxelwise whole‑brain results and provides no stereotactic (MNI/Talairach) coordinates or group-level voxelwise maps, so it fails I6 and I7. The paper does include clinically diagnosed bvFTD participants (counts reported) and meets the sample size requirement (I4 and I5). Because the analyses are region‑of‑interest (hippocampal subfields) with no whole‑brain voxelwise results, exclusion criterion E6 (ROI‑only analyses with no whole‑brain results) applies. Full text appears complete. Decision: EXCLUDE.

This is an empirical, whole-brain, voxel-wise longitudinal MRI study of frontotemporal lobar degeneration that includes a distinct bvFTD group (n=44) and controls (n=97). The methods use voxel-wise gray-matter contraction/expansion maps computed with SPM12 and DARTEL, normalized to MNI space, and report between-group t-maps and consensus voxelwise ROIs comparing bvFTD to controls. Sample sizes exceed the minimum. Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results for bvFTD versus controls are presented (figures, maps, and effect sizes). No exclusion criteria (e.g., review-only, ROI-only, seed-based FC/DTI/cortical-thickness-only) apply. Full text (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion) is provided. Therefore all required inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7, I8) are met and no exclusion criteria are triggered.

The study is excluded because it does not include a clinically diagnosed behavioral variant frontotemporal dementia (bvFTD) or Pick's disease group (I4 not met). Although it reports whole-brain VBM analyses of pathology-confirmed groups (FTLD-tau, TDP43A/C), the groups are defined by post-mortem pathology rather than a clinical bvFTD (or Pick) diagnostic group, and no between-group contrast is reported that specifically compares a clinically defined bvFTD group to controls in standard stereotactic space (I6 and I7 not met). The paper does satisfy imaging modality and sample size criteria (I3: VBM used; I5: patient groups have ≥6 subjects), and reports whole-brain voxelwise results for pathology groups, but these do not correspond to the target clinical diagnosis required by the review. No exclusion criteria from the list apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This study uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) and includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=12) and controls (n=21), meeting I3, I4 and the sample-size criterion I5. However, the VBM analyses reported are correlational (gray-matter correlations with conjunction-search accuracy) across the pooled sample and an ANOVA on extracted voxel values; the paper does not present a whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrast (bvFTD vs. controls) reported in MNI/Talairach space or coordinate tables that unambiguously reflect bvFTD-specific, group-level voxelwise results. Therefore it fails I6 and I7 (no clearly reported whole-brain between-group voxelwise contrast comparing bvFTD to controls). No exclusion criteria from the list apply. Because ALL inclusion criteria must be met, the study is excluded.

This is a single-family case series with one symptomatic bvFTD proband and some healthy mutation carriers. Imaging includes FDG-PET (so I3 met) and the proband is clinically diagnosed bvFTD (I4 met). However, the study does not meet required sample size (fewer than 6 bvFTD patients; I5 not met), has no control group and reports no between-group voxelwise contrasts in MNI/Talairach space (I6 not met), and provides no group-level whole-brain voxelwise results from a target bvFTD sample (I7 not met). Therefore it fails multiple mandatory inclusion criteria and must be excluded. Full text appears complete.

While the study includes FDG-PET imaging (I3), clinically diagnosed bvFTD participants (11 bvFTD patients; I4), and sufficient group sizes (bvFTD n=11; controls n=13; I5), it does not report any group-level, whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrasts in a standardized stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) comparing the bvFTD group to controls. The FDG-PET analysis was single-subject (each patient compared to a healthy control group) and correlations of exosomal HSP70 with the number of hypometabolic voxels were reported, but no group-level voxelwise results or coordinates are provided for the bvFTD group as a whole. Therefore inclusion criteria I6 and I7 are not satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) are triggered. Full text appears complete. Excluded on the basis of missing required group-level whole-brain voxelwise results (I6, I7 not met).

The study is excluded because it does not meet inclusion criterion I6. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (uses voxelwise T1-weighted MRI morphometry/WBGM, VBM-like processing with SPM12/DARTEL), I4 (includes clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD patients per consensus criteria), I5 (FTD group N=39, >6), I7 (reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise information in the form of 3D SVM weight maps), and I8 (whole-brain maps are presented as figures/slices). Inclusion criterion not met: I6 — the paper does not report at least one between-group contrast comparing the bvFTD group to healthy controls in a defined stereotaxic space (MNI/Talairach). Instead, comparisons are between patient groups (FTD vs AD subtypes or depression) and the reported maps are SVM-derived weight maps rather than mass-univariate between-group coordinate tables. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) were triggered. Full text appears complete.

This study is excluded because it reports only region-of-interest (ROI) volumetric analyses of cerebellar subregions using atlas segmentation and does not present voxel-based whole-brain (VBM), fMRI, or FDG-PET results. Exclusion criteria met: E6 (only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results). Inclusion criteria met: I4 (sample includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD participants within genetic groups) and I5 (patient groups and controls each have ≥6 participants). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (study does not use VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET; it uses T1 volumetric ROI segmentation), I6 (no reported between-group voxelwise contrasts in MNI/Talairach space comparing a bvFTD group to controls), and I7 (no whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results reported). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study is excluded because it does not meet the imaging-modality and whole-brain voxelwise reporting criteria required by the review. It uses structural MRI with region-based parcellation (SABRE) and multivariate partial least squares on regional volumes rather than VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET (I3 not met). The analyses are region-of-interest/parcellation-based and do not report whole-brain voxelwise group-level coordinates in standard stereotaxic space, nor between-group voxelwise contrasts for an unpooled bvFTD group (I6 and I7 not met). Inclusion criteria that are met: the sample includes clinically diagnosed FTD patients (per Neary criteria) and subgroup size meets the minimum (FTD n=8) with adequate control numbers (I4, I5 met). Exclusion criteria met: E6 (ROI-only analyses without whole-brain voxelwise results). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion).

The study uses whole-brain VBM and includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=15) and adequate control samples, but it does not report any voxelwise, between-group contrast that specifically compares a bvFTD-only group to healthy controls in stereotactic space. Instead, VBM analyses are reported for behavioral subgroups defined by storytelling characteristics (mixed diagnostic composition). Thus key inclusion criteria for this review are not met: no bvFTD-specific whole-brain (voxelwise) between-group results are provided. Exclusion criteria: none met.

This study used voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (I3 met) and included sufficient participant numbers (at least 6 patients and controls; I5 met). However, it does not meet key review requirements: participants are genetic FTD mutation carriers (symptomatic and presymptomatic) but the paper does not report a clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) group specifically (I4 NOT met). The paper does not report a between-group, voxelwise contrast comparing a bvFTD patient group to healthy controls in MNI/Talairach space (I6 NOT met), nor does it provide a whole-brain group-level voxelwise result attributable to a bvFTD sample (I7 NOT met). Full text appears complete. Therefore the study is excluded.

This study used T1 MRI with voxelwise processing (W-score maps) and then aggregated into regional (ROI) atrophy burdens, so imaging method meets I3. Sample sizes for patient and control groups exceed 6, so I5 is met. However, the paper does not specifically report results from clinically diagnosed bvFTD or Pick’s disease patients (participants are familial FTLD mutation carriers with heterogeneous clinical syndromes), so I4 is not met. The manuscript does not present whole-brain, group-level voxelwise between-group contrasts (in MNI/Talairach coordinates) comparing a bvFTD group to controls; results are reported as ROI-integrated scores and classifier weights rather than voxelwise coordinate tables/figures, so I6 and I7 are not met. Because only ROI-level results (integrated W-scores/region weights) are reported with no clear whole-brain voxelwise group contrasts, exclusion criterion E6 applies. Full text appears complete.

This study is excluded because it does not meet key inclusion criteria for the review. Although it uses an eligible imaging modality (FDG-PET; I3) and includes an FTLD patient subgroup with more than six patients (I5), it does not clearly report clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) or Pick's disease as required (I4 not met). The FTLD label in this paper is broad and the paper does not state that participants were diagnosed specifically with bvFTD. Critically, the paper does not report a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrast (bvFTD vs healthy controls) in standard stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) with coordinates; instead analyses focus on diagnostic classification (FDG SPM single-subject comparisons to a normative database) and between-dementia-group logistic/regression results (FTLD vs non-FTLD) without providing whole-brain group-level coordinate results for a bvFTD group (I6 and I7 not met). No exclusion criteria from the list are directly triggered. Therefore the paper must be excluded for failing to meet I4, I6 and I7.

This study is an ROI manual volumetry study of the putamen using structural T1 MRI, not VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET; it does not report any whole-brain, voxelwise results or coordinates (MNI/Talairach). Inclusion met: I4 (contains clinically diagnosed FTD subgroup likely corresponding to bvFTD) and I5 (patient and control groups exceed n>=6). Inclusion not met: I3 (imaging modality requirement), I6 (reporting between-group contrasts in standard coordinate space), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise result). Exclusion criterion E6 (ROI-only analyses with no whole-brain results) therefore applies. Full text appears complete.

The study is excluded because, although it uses VBM (I3) and has adequate group sizes (converters n=8; controls n≥35) satisfying I5, it does not provide group-level whole-brain voxelwise results specifically for a clinically diagnosed bvFTD-only patient group. The ‘converter’ group is pooled (includes both bvFTD and nfvPPA cases) and the reported voxelwise contrasts compare this pooled converter group to controls, so the paper does not meet: I4 (bvFTD-only sample), I6 (between-group contrast of bvFTD group vs controls without pooling), and I7 (whole-brain voxelwise result clearly identified as coming from a bvFTD target group). No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) are triggered. Full text is complete.

The study used FDG-PET (I3) and included >6 FTD patients and >6 controls (I5). The sample includes clinically diagnosed FTD subtypes, including behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) (I4). However, it does NOT report any between-group whole-brain (voxelwise) contrast in MNI/Talairach space comparing a bvFTD-only group to healthy controls (I6 not met). The reported PET result is a voxelwise correlation of metabolic rate with prosocial sexual behavior across combined patient groups (FTD and CBS), not a bvFTD vs control group-level contrast, and no whole-brain group-level voxelwise result is clearly identified as coming from a bvFTD-only group (I7 not met). Full text appears complete. Therefore the paper does not meet all required inclusion criteria for this bvFTD-focused meta-analysis.

This study uses structural volumetric MRI with FreeSurfer ROI analyses, not VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET, and it does not report whole-brain, voxelwise group contrasts comparing bvFTD to healthy controls. Inclusion met: I4 (bvFTD patients included; bvFTD n=26) and I5 (patient group size ≥6). Inclusion not met: I3 (imaging modality is not VBM/fMRI/FDG-PET), I6 (no between-group voxelwise contrasts comparing bvFTD to controls), I7 (no whole-brain voxelwise group-level results reported). Exclusion criteria met: E6 (only ROI/volumetric analyses with no whole-brain results). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the paper does not meet required imaging and whole-brain contrast criteria for inclusion.

This is an empirical VBM study that includes a subgroup (ALS-FTD) who met criteria for bvFTD and reports whole-brain voxelwise VBM (SPM/DARTEL) and TBSS results comparing that subgroup to controls; however the patient sample comprises individuals with ALS (a concurrent neurological disorder). This violates exclusion criterion E7 (samples with other neurological symptoms). Therefore the study must be excluded despite meeting the imaging and reporting criteria.

This is a single-case report (n=1) and does not meet several required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis. Specifically, only I3 is satisfied (FDG-PET used). The study does not meet I4 (the sample is a single patient described as 'FTLD-like' rather than a clinically diagnosed bvFTD/Pick’s disease group), I5 (fewer than 6 participants in the patient group), I6 (no between-group contrasts in MNI/Talairach space comparing a bvFTD group to controls), and I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise results). No exclusion criteria from the provided list apply. Full text appears complete.

This study used FDG-PET and includes an FTD patient group (n=13) and controls (n=26) with voxelwise, whole-brain (Talairach) group contrasts; however, it does not specify that the FTD cases are behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) or Pick’s disease. Inclusion criterion I4 (clinically diagnosed bvFTD or Pick’s disease) is not met, and therefore criterion I6 (between-group contrast specifically comparing a bvFTD group to controls) cannot be satisfied. All other applicable inclusion criteria were met (I3, I5, I7, I8). No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) apply. Full text appears complete. Exclusion is based on lack of specification of bvFTD/Pick diagnosis in the sample, so patient group does not meet the target diagnostic inclusion required by the review.

The study is excluded because it uses structural MRI morphometry (manual/automated segmentation and radial distance shape mapping of the putamen), not VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET, and reports ROI-based shape/volume analyses rather than whole-brain voxelwise results with stereotactic coordinates. (a) Exclusion criteria met: E6 (reports only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results). (b) Inclusion criteria met: I4 (includes clinically diagnosed behavioral variant FTD patients), I5 (sample sizes: FTD n=33, controls n=17). (c) Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (imaging modality is structural morphometry, not VBM/fMRI/FDG-PET), I6 (no between-group contrasts reported in MNI/Talairach coordinate space), I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise results reported). Full text appears complete for assessment.

This full text meets all required inclusion criteria: (I3) the study used voxel-based morphometry (VBM) for imaging analyses; (I4) it included a clinically diagnosed behavioural-variant frontotemporal dementia (bvFTD) group (n=20); (I5) group sizes meet sample thresholds (bvFTD=20; controls=20); (I6) the paper reports between-group voxelwise contrasts and states that maximum coordinates are reported in MNI space (i.e., results are presented in a defined stereotactic space) and bvFTD results are not pooled with other patient groups; (I7) whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results are described and used in voxel-based morphometry analyses; (I8) results/coordinates are reported and described (including overlap analyses). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, and is therefore complete for screening purposes. No exclusion criteria were met.

Although the study uses VBM (I3), includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients among its sample (I4), has adequate sample sizes (42 patients, 30 controls; I5), and reports whole-brain VBM results for pathologic groups (so reporting format is acceptable, I8), it does NOT report a between-group contrast that directly compares a clinically defined bvFTD group to controls (in MNI/Talairach space) where the bvFTD group is not pooled with other patient groups (I6). Likewise, it does not provide a whole-brain group-level voxelwise result clearly identified as coming from the bvFTD target sample (I7). No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) are met. Full text appears complete. Therefore the study must be excluded for failing to meet I6 and I7.

This study examines frontal-variant FTLD (fv-FTLD), equivalent to behavioral variant FTD, using 18FDG-PET (and [11C]MDL PET) with voxelwise SPM analyses. It reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (sb: whole fv-FTLD vs controls; apathetic vs controls; disinhibited vs controls; direct between-group contrasts) with coordinates in MNI space and cluster-level information. Patient group (n=18) and control group (n=24) meet sample-size thresholds; PET subgroup analyses included 8 patients and 6 controls (>=6). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (not a review, not ROI-only, no comorbid psychiatric/other dementia in sample, empirical FDG-PET whole-brain results reported). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the review.

This study used structural MRI with VBM-based preprocessing (I3 satisfied) and included an FTD patient group (n≈12) and healthy controls (n=18) meeting minimum sample sizes (I5 satisfied). However, it does not specify behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) or Pick’s disease specifically (I4 not met). Critically, the paper reports SVM-based multivariate classification results rather than mass-univariate, whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrasts with coordinates in MNI/Talairach space comparing bvFTD to controls; no group-level voxelwise results identified as coming from a bvFTD target sample are provided (I6 and I7 not met). Therefore it fails key inclusion criteria required for this review. No exclusion criteria from the list were triggered.

This is an open-label FDG-PET study in FTD that includes a bvFTD subgroup (n=7) and reports voxelwise, group-level PET results (before vs after memantine) with coordinates. However, it does not include any between-group contrasts comparing a bvFTD group to healthy controls in MNI/Talairach space. The meta-analysis requires at least one between-group contrast of bvFTD versus controls (I6). Therefore the study fails to meet inclusion criterion I6 and must be excluded.

This is an empirical MRI study of white matter hyperintensities using automated segmentation on T1/T2 images in genetic FTD cohorts. It does not use VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET (I3 not met). The paper reports mutation-defined symptomatic FTD groups but does not specify that participants are clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD or Pick’s disease (I4 not met). Results are reported as regional/zonal volumetric comparisons and summary plots rather than voxelwise, stereotactically-localized (MNI/Talairach) whole-brain coordinates; no voxelwise group-level coordinates are provided (I6 and I7 not met). The study does meet the sample size requirement (I5 met: patient and control groups ≥6). Because the analyses are region-based/zonal (no whole-brain voxelwise coordinate results), this falls under exclusion E6 (only ROI/region-based analyses with no whole-brain results). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical study of bvFTD using structural T1 MRI visual atrophy ratings and survival analysis. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample) and I5 (n=31 patients ≥6). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (does not use VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET — uses visual structural MRI ratings), I6 (no between-group voxelwise contrasts reported in MNI/Talairach space), and I7 (no whole-brain voxelwise group-level results). Exclusion criteria met: E6 (study does not report whole-brain voxelwise results; only region-like/visual rating measures). Therefore the study does not provide the required voxelwise whole-brain imaging results in the specified modalities and must be excluded.

This study is excluded because it does not provide voxelwise, whole-brain group-level contrasts comparing clinically diagnosed bvFTD (or Pick's disease) to controls, and thus does not meet key inclusion criteria. Exclusion criteria met: E6 (no whole-brain voxelwise results; analyses are clinical/visual and PALZ-based rather than reported voxelwise coordinates). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (uses FDG-PET), I5 (FTD patient group n=18 ≥6). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (sample is reported as ‘FTD’ but not specified as behavioral-variant FTD or Pick’s disease), I6 (no between-group contrast in MNI/Talairach space comparing bvFTD vs controls), I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise result reported). Full text appears complete.

This is a longitudinal, empirical study that used voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (SPM2 optimized/modulated VBM) to compare MSTD (Tau +3 intron 10 mutation) patients to age- and gender-matched controls. The VBM analysis included 7 early-stage MSTD patients (all clinically diagnosed with bvFTD) and 19 controls, meeting the sample-size requirement. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrasts with significant clusters and refers to stereotactic locations in supplementary Table 4 (i.e., coordinates in a defined stereotactic space). Whole-brain voxelwise results are clearly identified as coming from the bvFTD-target sample. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, review/meta-analysis, methods-only, or disallowed imaging modalities) are met.

Study uses VBM and includes bvFTD patients (11 bvFTD) with adequate sample sizes and reports voxelwise MNI coordinates for associations; however it does NOT report any between-group voxelwise contrast comparing the bvFTD group alone to healthy controls in MNI/Talairach space. VBM analyses were performed as correlations within the combined FTLD patient cohort (and significant inference was made using small-volume correction within pre-specified ROIs). Thus inclusion criteria I3, I4 and I5 are met, but I6 and I7 (require a between-group contrast in stereotactic space for the bvFTD group and at least one group-level whole-brain voxelwise result from the target sample) are not met. Additionally, the reported neuroimaging inference relied on small-volume/ROI correction rather than whole-brain group-level results, invoking exclusion criterion E6. Full text appears complete. Therefore the study is excluded.

Although the study uses VBM (I3) and includes pathologically and clinically characterized FTD cases including Pick disease (PiD) and many clinically diagnosed frontal-variant (fvFTD) cases (satisfying I4) and has sufficient group sizes overall and for PiD and controls (I5), it does NOT report a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrast specifically comparing a clinically defined behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD/fvFTD) group to controls (I6 not met). The VBM results are reported for pathologic subgroups (FTD-U, PiD, tau exon 10+16) rather than for a clinical bvFTD group, so the required whole-brain, between-group coordinates/results for bvFTD are not available (I7 not met). No exclusion criteria are triggered. Therefore the study must be excluded for the review focused on bvFTD whole-brain contrasts.

This study is excluded because it does not meet key imaging and analysis inclusion criteria. Exclusion ID met: E6 (study reports only region-based/ROI volumetric analyses focused on frontal lobes and does not present whole-brain, voxelwise results). Inclusion IDs met: I4 (includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients; n=18) and I5 (bvFTD group size ≥6). Inclusion IDs not met: I3 (imaging modality is structural T1-weighted MRI volumetry with multi-atlas regional segmentation, not VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET), I6 (no between-group contrast reported comparing bvFTD to healthy controls in standard stereotactic space; comparisons are between patient groups), and I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise results reported). Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false). Therefore the paper does not satisfy all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis and is excluded.

Full text shows this is an empirical VBM study enrolling bvFTD patients (7) and healthy controls (21), and reports whole-brain VBM and DTI results. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (VBM used), I4 (bvFTD patients included), I5 (patient and control groups ≥6). However, the paper does not report a voxelwise between-group contrast comparing bvFTD patients directly to controls in MNI/Talairach space, nor does it report whole-brain group-level voxelwise results that are clearly identified as coming from the bvFTD group alone (results are correlational across participants and conjunctions across measures). Therefore inclusion criteria I6 and I7 are not met. No exclusion criteria (E5,E6,E7,E8,E9) appear to apply. Full text appears complete.

This full-text reports an empirical resting-state fMRI study (with VBM structural analysis) comparing clinically diagnosed probable bvFTD (n=25) to controls (n=29) and AD (n=31). It uses voxel-wise, whole-brain analyses (dual regression and voxel-wise permutation testing) with results presented in MNI-152 space and FWE-corrected TFCE statistics, and describes voxelwise group-level contrasts (bvFTD vs controls and bvFTD vs AD). Sample sizes exceed the minimum. The paper provides whole-brain voxelwise results clearly identified as coming from the bvFTD sample. No exclusion criteria (e.g., review-only, ROI-only, seed-only, DTI-only, comorbid psychiatric sample issues) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, conclusion). Therefore it meets all required inclusion criteria for the review.

This study does not meet the review’s target-sample and whole-brain contrast requirements. It includes FTLD patients (N=31) and uses 18F-FDG PET (I3 satisfied) and has sufficient patient sample size (I5 satisfied). However, it does not specify that the FTLD sample is clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) or Pick’s disease (I4 not met: FTLD is reported generally without bvFTD/Pick’s subgroup breakdown). The paper also does not report any between-group voxelwise contrast in stereotaxic space (MNI/Talairach) comparing a bvFTD group to controls (I6 not met) and therefore provides no group-level, whole-brain voxelwise result clearly identified as coming from a bvFTD target sample (I7 not met). No exclusion criteria from the list (E5–E9) are triggered. Because ALL inclusion criteria must be met and several are not, the study must be excluded.

(a) Exclusion criteria met: E6 — the study reports lobar/ROI volumetry (temporal and frontal lobe volumes and ratios) and does not present whole-brain voxelwise results or coordinate tables. 
(b) Inclusion criteria met: I3 — uses automated voxel-based volumetry (SPM5-based voxel approach akin to VBM); I4 — includes a bvFTLD subgroup (6 bvFTLD patients); I5 — sample sizes meet thresholds (bvFTLD n=6; controls n=30). 
(c) Inclusion criteria not met: I6 — no report of at least one between-group voxelwise contrast in a defined stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) comparing the bvFTLD group to controls unpooled; I7 — no group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) result clearly identified for the target group. 
Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, conclusion). Therefore the study is excluded because it provides only ROI/lobar volumetry without whole-brain voxelwise contrasts required by the review.

This is an empirical VBM study of bvFTD cases (both C9ORF72 carriers and sporadic bvFTD) including healthy controls. It reports whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrasts (patient groups vs Controls) using MNI space and provides coordinates/figures (including supplementary table). Sample sizes meet the minimum (C9 n=8, sporadic bvFTD n=15, Controls n=15). Whole-brain group-level results for the target bvFTD groups are clearly identified. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion and imaging details; therefore judged complete.

Although this study uses whole-brain VBM in MNI space and includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=18) with adequate control numbers, the provided full text does not report any between-group voxelwise contrast directly comparing the bvFTD group to healthy controls in standard space. It does report within-group whole-brain VBM covariate results for bvFTD (VBM correlations with IGT scores) but no explicit bvFTD vs. control voxelwise contrast coordinates/results are presented in the supplied text. Therefore inclusion criterion I6 (at least one between-group contrast comparing bvFTD to controls) is not satisfied. Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4, I5, I7, I8. No exclusion criteria were triggered.

While this study uses FDG-PET (I3), includes clinically diagnosed frontal-variant FTD patients (equivalent to bvFTD; I4), has sufficient patient sample size (n=70; I5), and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise component images in MNI space (I7, acceptable reporting format I8), it does not present a between-group voxelwise contrast comparing the bvFTD/fv-FTD group directly to healthy controls in MNI or Talairach space (criterion I6). The paper focuses on within-group PCA decomposition of patient scans rather than reporting a between-group coordinate-based contrast vs controls; therefore it fails to meet inclusion criterion I6 and must be excluded. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) are triggered. Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

The study used VBM and resting-state fMRI (I3) and included clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (7 bvFTD cases within the FTD-GRN+ group) (I4). Sample sizes meet minimums (14 patients, control groups ≥6) (I5). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise group results (VBM and functional maps) (I7) and presents results in figures/tables (I8). However, the critical requirement I6 is not met: the reported between-group contrasts compare a combined FTD-GRN+ group (mixing bvFTD and avPPA) to controls rather than reporting a bvFTD-only versus control whole-brain contrast. The bvFTD subgroup is pooled with other FTD phenotypes in the main analyses, so no bvFTD-specific whole-brain contrast is available. No exclusion criteria were triggered. Therefore the study is excluded for failing inclusion criterion I6.

This empirical study used Voxel-Based Morphometry (VBM) (and TBSS/DTI) as imaging modalities and explicitly included a clinically diagnosed bvFTD patient group (n=10) and healthy controls (n=26). The bvFTD patient group meets the minimum sample size requirement (>=6) and controls also exceed the minimum (>=6). The paper reports that separate VBM group-level analyses were run for each patient group (including bvFTD) versus healthy controls and refers to results/coordinates reported in the Supplementary Information (S11), satisfying the requirement for at least one between-group, whole-brain (voxelwise) contrast in stereotactic space. Whole-brain VBM and TBSS results (with cluster/peak reporting and FWE-corrected thresholds) are described in the text and figures, and the authors note coordinates/peaks and use standard MNI space. Supplementary materials are acceptable per inclusion rules. Given these points, the study meets all specified inclusion criteria for the bvFTD meta-analysis. Confidence is somewhat reduced because some between-group coordinate tables are reported in Supplementary Information rather than the main text, but the manuscript clearly indicates those whole-brain contrasts were performed and reported.

This study is excluded because it reports primarily ROI- and summary-index-based imaging results and does not present whole-brain, voxelwise group-level coordinate results required for inclusion. Exclusion ID met: E6 (reports only ROI/summary analyses with no clear whole-brain voxelwise results). Inclusion IDs met: I3 (uses FDG-PET and VBM-derived indices). Inclusion IDs not met: I4 (unclear whether the FTD sample is specifically behavioral variant FTD or Pick's disease — the paper reports FTD broadly and mentions subtypes but does not specify bvFTD cases), I5 (FTD subgroup size is not provided in the provided text — cannot verify >=6 patients in the bvFTD/Pick's group), I6 (no reported between-group contrasts in stereotactic space specifically comparing bvFTD to controls), I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise results identified). Full text appears complete for screening (fulltext_incomplete: false).

This study used Voxel-Based Morphometry (VBM) (satisfies I3) and includes sufficient participant numbers across patient and control groups (satisfies I5). However, it does not report results specifically for clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) or Pick's disease patients: the sample lists participants with “frontotemporal dementia (FTD)” but does not specify behavioral-variant FTD or provide a bvFTD-only group (I4 not met). Consequently, there are no between-group whole-brain contrasts comparing a bvFTD group to controls (I6 not met), and no group-level whole-brain results clearly identified as coming from a bvFTD sample (I7 not met). Full text appears complete. Therefore the paper is excluded because it fails to meet I4, I6, and I7.

This is an empirical VBM study that reports voxelwise group contrasts with coordinates comparing FTD patients to controls. Imaging modality: VBM (meets I3). Sample: includes clinically diagnosed FTD patients meeting Neary criteria and behavioral descriptions consistent with behavioral-variant FTD (meets I4). Sample sizes exceed thresholds (32 patients total, 27 with usable MRI; 47 controls) satisfying I5. The paper reports between-group voxelwise contrasts (overeating FTD subgroup vs nonovereaters and controls) with stereotactic coordinates (MNI/Talairach reported), satisfying I6 and I8. VBM analyses are voxelwise/group-level whole-brain comparisons within an a priori ROI and results are clearly identified as coming from the target patient group (meets I7). No exclusion criteria apply (not a review, not ROI-only without voxelwise results, not only FC/DTI/thickness, and no disqualifying comorbid sample issues). Note: the authors use the term “FTD” and Neary criteria rather than explicitly ‘bvFTD’; behavioral descriptions and diagnostic criteria indicate behavioral-variant FTD, which slightly reduces but does not preclude inclusion. Overall confidence 0.85.

This is an empirical FDG-PET study that specifically investigates bvFTD. It includes clinically and pathologically diagnosed bvFTD participants (Center-A and Center-B) with patient group sizes well above 6 and multiple healthy control groups (n≥6). The imaging data were normalized to MNI space and analyzed voxelwise using spatial covariance/PCA yielding whole-brain topographies (bFDRP) reported and visualized; group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results are explicitly described and attributed to the bvFTD group. Results are presented in figures and described in MNI-normalized space; bootstrap/voxelwise statistics and thresholds are reported. The paper is original empirical research (not a review), does not rely solely on ROI analyses, and does not fall under excluded modalities. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (I3,I4,I5,I6,I7,I8) and no exclusion criteria are met.

This study used FDG-PET (I3 satisfied) and included an FTLD patient group of n=11 (I5 satisfied). However it does not report clinically labeled bvFTD/Pick’s disease explicitly (I4 not clearly met), and crucially it does not provide whole-brain, voxelwise group-level results in a standard stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) comparing bvFTD to healthy controls; results are reported as regional/ROI hypometabolism counts and pattern descriptions rather than voxelwise coordinates (I6 and I7 not met). Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E6 (only ROI/regional analyses without whole-brain voxelwise results). Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This is an empirical study that uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) and reports whole-brain, voxelwise group comparisons in MNI space. It includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample (n=13) and healthy controls (n=12), meeting sample-size requirements. The paper provides between-group contrasts (bvFTD vs. controls) with anatomical localization and MNI coordinates, and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise results and neuroanatomical correlates of emotional memory. The full text includes introduction, methods (VBM acquisition and preprocessing), results (group VBM comparisons and correlations) and discussion, so the provided full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the review.

This study uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) on whole-brain T1-weighted MRI and reports voxelwise group comparisons with MNI coordinates. The ALS-FTD subgroup (n=18) met clinical Neary criteria for FTD and predominantly showed behavioral abnormalities consistent with bvFTD; neurologic disease controls (n=15) are included. VBM whole-brain results (voxelwise, corrected p<0.05) are reported for ALS-FTD versus controls and versus other ALS subgroups and coordinate tables (MNI) are provided. Sample sizes exceed the minimum (patient and control groups ≥6). The full text (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion) is present; supplementary material being online is acceptable. Therefore all relevant inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

Although the study used FDG-PET (meets I3), it does not provide a group-level, whole-brain between-group contrast specifically for behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD). The FTLD sample is pooled (FTD N=3, SD N=6, mixed N=4) and the paper presents comparisons of FTLD (pooled) and AD versus SCI controls rather than a separate bvFTD (FTD) versus control contrast. The number of bvFTD/FTD cases is only 3 (<6), so the bvFTD patient group does not meet the minimum sample size (I5). Therefore the study fails I4 (target sample not separably reported as bvFTD), I5 (bvFTD group <6), I6 (no bvFTD-vs-control whole-brain contrast where bvFTD are not pooled), and I7 (no whole-brain result clearly identified as coming from a bvFTD target group).

Study uses VBM and includes a clinically defined FTD (bvFTD) subgroup (n=47) and healthy controls (n=43), meeting imaging and sample-size criteria. However, the neuroimaging analyses report whole-brain voxelwise correlations of interpersonal traits across a mixed diagnostic sample and co-atrophy checks; the paper does not present any between-group, whole-brain (voxelwise) contrast or group-level VBM result specifically comparing the bvFTD (FTD variant) group to controls in MNI/Talairach space. Therefore it fails to meet I6 and I7 (bvFTD-specific between-group, whole-brain results). No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) apply. Excluded on the basis of missing bvFTD-specific whole-brain between-group results.

This study includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=18) and uses 18F-FDG PET (I4, I3) with at least 6 patients in the bvFTD group (I5). It reports voxel-wise, whole-brain PET analyses relating metabolism to oculomotor parameters (results depicted in figures and described in text) (I8). However, it does not present any between-group, whole-brain (voxelwise) contrast directly comparing the bvFTD group to healthy controls in stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach). The FDG-PET results are correlational analyses across a combined patient set (n=18) and the controls do not appear to have FDG-PET data for group comparison; no bvFTD vs. control voxelwise contrast or coordinate table is reported. Therefore inclusion criteria I6 and I7 are not met, so the study must be excluded.

This is an empirical VBM study that compares a clinically defined frontotemporal dementia (FTD) patient group (behaviorally defined FTD; patients with predominant behavioral/frontal syndrome, excluding progressive aphasia/semantic dementia) to healthy controls using whole-brain, voxelwise SPM analyses. Imaging modality is VBM (I3). The patient sample includes 9 FTD participants and 26 controls, meeting the minimum N≥6 for both groups (I5). Between-group voxelwise contrasts are reported in stereotactic space (SPM coordinates; e.g., periaqueductal gray at (0,-28,-10)) and whole-brain group-level voxelwise results are presented and attributed to the FTD sample (I6, I7). Results are reported as corrected and uncorrected voxelwise findings and coordinates (I8). No exclusion criteria (reviews-only, ROI-only, non-empirical, DTI/FC/CTh-only, or prohibited comorbid-sample) are met. Full text appears complete (includes intro, methods, results, discussion).

This is a resting-state fMRI study that includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients, but it does not provide voxelwise whole-brain (MNI/Talairach) between-group contrasts for a bvFTD-only group. The bvFTD-only subgroup has N=3 (<6), and bvFTD patients are pooled with ALS-FTD in subgroup analyses (bvFTD+ n=9), so there is no unpooled bvFTD vs. control voxelwise result. Analyses are ROI/parcellation-based graph/network metrics (82 VOIs) and edge/hub results rather than whole-brain voxelwise coordinates, so it meets exclusion E6 (ROI-only/no whole-brain results). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (resting-state fMRI modality) and I4 (includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (bvFTD patient group <6 for bvFTD-only), I6 (no between-group voxelwise contrast comparing bvFTD-only to controls), I7 (no whole-brain voxelwise group-level result in stereotactic space). Full text appears complete.

This study meets all inclusion criteria: it uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (I3); includes a clinically diagnosed behavioral/dysexecutive FTLD subgroup (bvFTLD) with n=71 and an imaging subset bvFTLD n=51 (I4, I5); reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level contrasts in MNI space comparing bvFTLD to healthy controls (contrasted with ~42 controls) and provides peak coordinates/tables and figures (I6, I7, I8). The full text includes methods, results, and discussion, enabling assessment of voxelwise whole-brain results. No exclusion criteria are met (not a review, not ROI-only, not seed-based FC/DTI/cortical thickness only, and comorbidities were excluded per methods).

The study reports whole-brain voxel-based morphometry (VBM) analyses (I3) and includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample (31 patients) (I4) with an adequate sample size (31 bvFTD; 56 controls) meeting the ≥6 participant threshold (I5). It provides group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts comparing bvFTD to controls and reports results on the Montreal Neurological Institute standard brain (MNI) with statistical parametric maps and coordinate-based tables/figures (I6, I7, I8). No exclusion criteria apply (not a review, not ROI-only, not seed-FC/DTI/cortical-thickness only, and no evidence of disallowed comorbid sample). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical study that used task-based BOLD fMRI and voxel-based morphometric (VBM) volumetric MRI analyses comparing bvFTD patients to healthy controls. The sample includes 16 clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients and 16 healthy seniors (both ≥6). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise group contrasts (bvFTD vs. controls) using SPM8 with FDR-corrected thresholds and cluster extent, and presents overlapping ROIs and coordinates (reported in figures/tables) in a standard stereotactic space. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all required inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7, I8) and violates none of the exclusion criteria.

This study uses voxel-based morphometry (SPM99 VBM) and includes a behavioral-variant-like subgroup (SOC/EXEC), with sufficient sample sizes (FTD-related n=73; controls n=13). Inclusion criterion I6 (a between-group contrast comparing bvFTD to controls) is therefore not met. Accordingly, the study must be excluded.

This study uses VBM and includes a clinically-diagnosed FTD subgroup with adequate sample size, but it does not report any between-group, whole-brain (voxelwise) contrasts directly comparing the bvFTD/FTD group to healthy controls in MNI/Talairach space. Excluded because the study does not use the required imaging modalities (it uses FreeSurfer regional volumetry and cortical thickness, not VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET — violates I3), does not specifically include clinically diagnosed behavioral variant FTD or Pick's disease (FTD group is general, not clearly bvFTD — violates I4), and does not report whole-brain voxelwise, coordinate-based contrasts in standard (MNI/Talairach) space comparing a bvFTD group to controls (violates I6 and I7). The study used FDG-PET and SPM5 and included an FTD patient group (n=7) with healthy controls (n=18), so imaging modality (I3) and sample size (I5) criteria are met. This study meets the review objective and all required inclusion criteria. The paper reports between-group voxelwise contrasts (patients/subgroups vs controls) with peak voxels/tables and figures in MNI space (I6, I8). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study uses whole-brain VBM and includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD subgroup (n=58) with controls (n=44), but its reported voxelwise analyses are brain–behavior correlations across a pooled neurodegenerative sample rather than between-group voxelwise contrasts comparing bvFTD to controls. The paper does not present a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) result clearly identified as coming solely from the bvFTD group (no bvFTD vs control contrast in MNI/Talairach space reported). Therefore it fails inclusion criteria I6 and I7 despite meeting I3, I4, and I5. No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

The study is excluded because it does not meet imaging and whole-brain reporting criteria required for the review. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (participants: clinically diagnosed FTD patients per Neary criteria, with semantic dementia and PNFA excluded, consistent with bvFTD sampling) and I5 (sample sizes: FTD n=44, controls present). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (imaging modality) — the study used structural MRI lobar volumetry and automated regional volumes, not VBM, task/resting fMRI, or FDG-PET; I6 (between-group voxelwise contrasts in MNI/Talairach) — no voxelwise coordinate-based group contrasts are reported; I7 (whole-brain voxelwise group-level result from target sample) — not provided. Exclusion criteria triggered: E6 (reports only ROI/lobar analyses with no whole-brain voxelwise results). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).
