This study meets the review objective and all required inclusion criteria: it uses resting-state fMRI and voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (I3); includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (probable bvFTD) (I4); has adequate sample size (44 patients, 60 controls) exceeding the 6-participant minimum (I5); reports group-level VBM comparisons of bvFTD versus controls (whole-brain, voxelwise contrasts consistent with VBM methods) satisfying between-group contrast reporting in standard (voxelwise) space (I6); and provides whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results identified as coming from the bvFTD group (I7). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) apply: this is an empirical study (not a review), reports whole-brain VBM (not ROI-only), participants had no major comorbid psychiatric/neurological disorders, and it does not only report seed-based FC/DTI/cortical thickness. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This study meets inclusion criteria I3 (uses VBM), I4 (includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD participants within the sample: 47 bvFTD), and I5 (sample sizes: bvFTD n=47, controls n=34, both ≥6). However it does NOT meet I6 and I7: the published whole-brain VBM results are correlational analyses within the combined FTD patient sample (atrophy correlated with happiness behavior) rather than a between-group voxelwise contrast comparing a bvFTD group to healthy controls in MNI/Talairach space. No group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results are reported that are clearly identified as coming from the bvFTD group alone (bvFTD results are not presented as an independent between-group contrast vs controls). Full text appears complete. Therefore the study must be excluded for failing to meet I6 and I7.

The study is excluded because it reports only ROI/parcellation-based metabolic connectivity analyses (60 AAL VOIs) and does not present any whole-brain, voxelwise, coordinate-based (MNI/Talairach) between-group contrasts for behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) versus controls. The FTLD group is analyzed as a pooled group including behavioral and language variants, and bvFTD-specific results are not reported separately. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (FDG-PET imaging), I4 (includes behavioral-variant FTLD patients within the sample), I5 (sample sizes meet minimums). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no between-group, coordinate-based voxelwise contrasts reported comparing bvFTD separately to controls), I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise results). Exclusion criteria met: E6 (study reports only ROI/parcellation-based analyses with no whole-brain voxelwise results). Full text appears complete.

Excluded because study does not meet key imaging and analysis inclusion criteria. Although it includes clinically diagnosed FTD patients (meets I4) and has sufficient patient sample size (72; meets I5), it does not use VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET (I3 not met), reports no between-group voxelwise contrasts in MNI/Talairach space comparing bvFTD to controls (I6 not met), and provides no group-level whole-brain voxelwise results (I7 not met). Full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria from the list (E5–E9) directly apply, but failure to meet the above inclusion criteria mandates exclusion.

This is an empirical study of sleep/activity (actigraphy and sleep diaries) in bvFTD patients—not an imaging study. Inclusion met: I4 (subjects are clinically diagnosed bvFTD) and I5 (patient group n=13; control groups ≥6). Inclusion not met: I3 (does not use VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET), I6 (no between-group voxelwise contrast in MNI/Talairach space), and I7 (no whole-brain voxelwise results reported). No exclusion criteria from the list apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Thus the paper does not meet all required imaging/whole-brain outcome criteria for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical multicenter 18F-FDG PET study that includes a frontal-variant FTD group (frontal variant = behavioral variant FTD), with 98 FTD patients and 110 controls (meets sample size criterion). Scans were spatially normalized to the Talairach atlas and analyzed voxelwise (Neurostat, 3D-SSP maps, voxelwise Z scores), producing group-level whole-brain results comparing FTD (frontal variant) to controls and to other dementia groups. Results for the FTD group are reported separately (not pooled) and presented as voxelwise/whole-brain maps and group comparisons. Full text includes methods, results, and discussion. Therefore the study satisfies imaging modality (FDG-PET), diagnostic group (frontal/bvFTD), sufficient sample size, and reports whole-brain Talairach-space voxelwise group results for bvFTD vs controls.

This is a case series of a PGRN-mutation family using structural MRI (qualitative) and neuropathology, not VBM/fMRI/FDG-PET. (a) Exclusion IDs met: none of the explicit exclusion criteria (E5-E9) strictly apply. (b) Inclusion IDs met: I4 (participants included clinically diagnosed FTD cases, including behavioral presentations). (c) Inclusion IDs NOT met: I3 (imaging modality is structural MRI, not VBM/fMRI/FDG-PET), I5 (imaging/neuroimaging sample with analyzable data is <6 participants for the modalities required), I6 (no between-group voxelwise contrasts in MNI/Talairach coordinates comparing bvFTD to controls), I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise results). The full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study does not meet the meta-analysis inclusion criteria and is excluded.

The study is excluded because it does not meet key bvFTD-specific inclusion criteria. Although it uses VBM (I3 satisfied) and has adequate group sizes (FTD n=9, controls n=10; I5 satisfied), it does not include a clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) or Pick’s disease group explicitly (I4 not met). The VBM analysis was a covariate-only correlation across all diagnostic groups rather than a between-group, voxelwise contrast comparing a bvFTD group to controls (I6 not met) and therefore does not provide whole-brain group-level results from a target bvFTD sample (I7 not met). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). No exclusion criteria from the review were triggered.

The study meets all required inclusion criteria: it uses Voxel-Based Morphometry (VBM) (I3); includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (7 participants) (I4) with a healthy control group (40) (I5); reports whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrasts in MNI space for individual phenotypes (including bvFTD vs controls) (I6, I7) and presents results in figures/text (I8). The full text provided contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete is false. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) are met.

This study is excluded because, although it uses VBM (I3) and includes clinically-diagnosed bvFTD/Pick’s patients (I4), it does not report a whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrast specifically comparing a bvFTD group (not pooled with other FTD subtypes) to controls in stereotactic coordinates. Thus it fails I6 and I7. The bvFTD subgroup sample size for a standalone bvFTD vs control contrast is not reported clearly, so I5 is not confirmed. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) are triggered. Full text appears complete.

EXCLUDED: The study uses FDG-PET (I3) and has adequate group sizes (FTLD n=13; controls n=10) meeting I5, but it does not report data specifically from clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) or Pick's disease—patients are described as FTLD without specification of bvFTD (I4 not met). Although voxelwise, whole-brain analyses are reported for FTLD vs controls, the paper does not provide results that can be clearly identified as coming from a bvFTD group, nor does it present between-group contrasts in a defined stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) for a bvFTD group (I6, I7 not met). Coordinate reporting or bvFTD-specific whole-brain results are not present in the provided full text (I8 not met). No exclusion criteria were triggered (none applicable). Full text appears complete.

Excluded because the study used manual region-of-interest volumetry (manual cortical parcellation) rather than VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET, and it reports ROI volumetric comparisons rather than whole-brain voxelwise results in stereotaxic coordinate space. This violates inclusion criteria I3 (required imaging modalities), I6 and I7 (required between-group voxelwise results in MNI/Talairach and whole-brain evidence). The study meets I5 (patient and control group sizes ≥6). The sample is described as FTD but not explicitly as behavioral variant FTD (bvFTD) or Pick’s disease, so I4 is not clearly satisfied. Exclusion criterion E6 (ROI-only analyses without whole-brain results) applies. Inclusion criteria met: I5. Inclusion criteria not met: I3, I4 (not specified as bvFTD), I6, I7. Exclusion criteria applied: E6. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical 18F-FDG PET study using voxel-wise SPM analysis (whole-brain) comparing 29 clinically diagnosed FTD patients to 11 healthy controls. The sample (n=29) meets the minimum size, and the authors explicitly excluded language variants (progressive nonfluent aphasia, semantic dementia), indicating the sample represents behavioral/clinical FTD cases. Analyses were performed in stereotactic space (normalized to MNI and coordinates converted to Talairach) and report group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results with peak coordinates (Table 3 and figures). All required inclusion criteria are met (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7, I8). No exclusion criteria apply (not a review, not ROI-only, not non-empirical, no disallowed modalities). The provided full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete is false.

Although the study uses VBM (I3), includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=28) (I4), and meets sample-size requirements for patients and controls (I5), it does not present any between-group voxelwise contrast comparing the bvFTD group directly to healthy controls in MNI/Talairach space (I6 not met). The VBM results are regression-based across a pooled, mixed-diagnosis sample (polisher/neutral and tarnisher/neutral analyses) and do not report group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results coming specifically from the bvFTD subgroup (I7 not met). Full text appears complete.

The study is excluded because it does not use an acceptable imaging modality (I3 not met) and does not report any coordinate-based, voxelwise whole-brain between-group contrasts (I6 and I7 not met). It uses conventional structural MRI visual/region ratings (exemplar-based atrophy scores across 12 areas) rather than VBM, FDG‑PET, or fMRI, and presents region-level atrophy ratings rather than whole-brain voxelwise results; this meets exclusion criterion E6 (ROI/region-only analyses with no whole-brain results). The paper does include clinically diagnosed frontotemporal dementia cases (meets I4) and has sufficient patient sample size (meets I5), but critical imaging and reporting criteria for inclusion (I3, I6, I7) are not satisfied. Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

Full text appears incomplete and consists mainly of references; the article appears to be a narrative review rather than an original empirical study. This study meets the review objective and all required inclusion criteria: imaging modality is FDG-PET (I3); the sample comprises clinically diagnosed frontotemporal dementia patients per Lund–Manchester criteria with other FTLD variants (semantic dementia, non-fluent progressive aphasia) excluded, consistent with a behavioral-variant FTD sample (I4) — diagnosis based on clinical criteria and PET pattern; sample sizes meet minimums (29 patients, 16 controls) (I5); the paper reports between-group voxelwise contrasts comparing FTD to controls with coordinates reported in Talairach/MNI space (I6); whole-brain, voxelwise group-level SPM results are clearly identified as coming from the patient group (I7); results are reported as coordinates/figures and described in text (I8). The provided full text includes introduction, methods, results, discussion and appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false). No exclusion criteria were met.

This study used VBM (I3), included a social/dysexecutive (SOC/EXEC) FTLD subgroup consistent with behavioral variant FTD (bvFTD) (I4), and the patient (SOC/EXEC n=17) and control (n=12) group sizes meet the sample-size criterion (I5). However, the paper does not report any group-level between-group voxelwise contrasts in a standard stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) comparing the bvFTD/SOC-EXEC group to controls (I6 not met). It also does not present a group-level whole-brain voxelwise result clearly identified as coming from the target bvFTD sample (I7 not met). The imaging approach is primarily subject-level VBM maps intersected with BA ROIs and subsequent ROI-based analyses, so it effectively lacks reported whole-brain group contrasts and therefore falls under exclusion E6 (ROI-only/no whole-brain group results). Consequently, the study is excluded.

The study reports whole-brain, voxelwise FDG-PET SPM analyses comparing FTD groups to controls and has adequate sample sizes (FTD n=29; controls n=11; FTD/MND n=8). However, the paper does not explicitly state that the patient sample consists of clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) or Pick's disease. The diagnostic label used is the consensus clinical diagnostic criteria for FTD (Neary et al.), but subtype breakdown (bvFTD vs other FTD variants) is not provided for the main FTD group. Inclusion criterion I4 (explicit bvFTD or Pick's disease sample) is therefore not met, and I6 (a between-group contrast explicitly of bvFTD versus controls) cannot be confirmed. No exclusion criteria from the provided list are triggered.

This study uses FDG-PET and includes >6 FTD patients overall, but it does not specifically report clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) or Pick’s disease as a clearly identified target group (I4 not met). The paper reports multivariate classification/discriminative images after MNI normalization, but it does not provide an explicit between-group voxelwise contrast (with coordinates) that compares a bvFTD group to controls in MNI/Talairach space (I6 not met). It is therefore not possible to confirm that a whole-brain, group-level voxelwise result from a bvFTD-only sample is reported (I7 not met). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (FDG-PET modality) and I5 (sample sizes >=6 across groups). No exclusion criteria from the list apply. Conclusion: EXCLUDED because key inclusion criteria I4, I6, and I7 are not satisfied.

This is a structural MRI study using voxel-wise morphometric analyses (SPM12) reporting voxelwise maps and coordinates in standard space, and has adequate group sizes, but it does NOT target clinically diagnosed bvFTD/Pick’s disease groups or report a between-group contrast of a bvFTD group versus controls. Specifically: (a) Inclusion criteria met: I3 (voxel-wise morphometry/VBM-like analysis), I5 (patient and control group sizes ≥6), I8 (coordinates reported in standard space/supplement). No exclusion criteria from the review were triggered. Therefore the paper should be excluded for not meeting the review’s target-sample and contrast requirements.

This study meets the review objective and inclusion criteria: it uses FDG-PET (I3), includes clinically diagnosed frontotemporal dementia patients consistent with behavioral-variant FTD (FTD subgroup) (I4), has adequate sample sizes (17 patients, 9 controls) exceeding the minimum of 6 per group (I5), and reports whole-brain, voxelwise SPM group analyses comparing FTD and SD to controls (unpooled FTD vs controls) (I6,I7). The paper presents voxelwise, whole-brain results (BA labels and cluster reporting) and refers to tables/figures for coordinates, which satisfies acceptable reporting formats (I8). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete with methods, results, and discussion provided.

This study is excluded because it does not meet required imaging and analysis criteria for the meta-analysis. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I6, and I7 are not met, and exclusion criterion E6 (studies with only ROI/regional analyses and no whole-brain results) applies. This is an empirical study that includes FDG-PET and an FTD patient group (n=10), so it meets I3 (FDG-PET) and I5 (≥6 patients). The full text also does not explicitly state that the FTD subgroup consists of clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) or Pick’s disease. Therefore it fails key inclusion criteria I4, I6, and I7 and meets exclusion criterion E6 (no whole-brain/voxelwise results).

(a) Exclusion criteria met: E6 — the study performs ROI/VOI-based feature extraction using the AAL parcellation and reports machine-learning classification (accuracy, sensitivity, specificity) rather than any group-level whole-brain voxelwise statistical contrasts or coordinate tables in MNI/Talairach space. The study reports VBM and DTI analyses in clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients and controls with MNI coordinates provided (I3, I4, I5, I6 satisfied). The study uses FDG-PET imaging (I3), includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (6 in template creation and 24 in validation) meeting the minimum group size (I4, I5). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study is excluded because it does not address behavioral variant frontotemporal dementia (bvFTD). Exclusion IDs met: none. This study is excluded because it does not target behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) as required. (a) Exclusion IDs met: none. (b) Inclusion IDs met: I3 (uses FDG-PET imaging). This study uses voxelwise structural MRI analysis (RAVENS/voxel-based methods) and reports whole-brain voxelwise results, includes clinically diagnosed FTD patients (including behavioral variant cases), and has adequate sample sizes (12 patients, 12 controls). This is an empirical, multimodal imaging study that includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=39) and healthy controls (n=61), uses whole-brain voxel-based morphometry (VBM) analyses in MNI space, and reports group-level, voxelwise comparisons and coordinates correlating gray matter with behavioral measures. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the review.

This study uses 18F-FDG PET (meets I3) but does not meet multiple other inclusion criteria required for a bvFTD meta-analysis. The study is excluded because it does not use VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET (it uses manual ROI volumetric MRI measures) and does not report any whole-brain, voxelwise group-level results in a standard stereotactic space. Although the study includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=84) and uses whole-brain VBM (I3, I4, I5 satisfied) and reports voxelwise results/coordinates (I8 satisfied), it does not report any between-group contrast comparing a bvFTD group to healthy controls (no control group or bvFTD-vs-control voxelwise contrast). This study used FDG-PET (meets I3) and includes patient and control groups >6 participants (meets I5). This is a single-case longitudinal case report of a patient with behavioral-variant FTD using structural MRI volumetry and manual segmentations; it does not use VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET at the group level, nor does it report group-level between-group voxelwise contrasts in standard (MNI/Talairach) space. Full text appears complete.

Although this empirical paper uses VBM (I3) and includes a clinically diagnosed frontal variant FTD subgroup (behavioral variant FTLD/FTD) with n=14 and a control group with n=20 (I4, I5 satisfied), it does not report a whole-brain, group-level voxelwise between-group contrast in MNI/Talairach space that isolates the bvFTD (FTD) group versus controls. The VBM analyses reported are correlational (brain volume correlated with antisaccade performance) and, importantly, the primary VBM models controlled for or used a combined FTLD group (FTD+SD+PA) rather than presenting a direct bvFTD (FTD) >/< control voxelwise contrast.
